org: OpenAI (Chen et al.; affiliation not shown on the arXiv abstract page)
tests: Writing a Python function from a docstring; checked by hidden unit tests.
questions: 164 (from the paper body; not re-verified on the abstract page I fetched)
format: Code generation: function signature + docstring in, Python function out
scoring: pass@k via unit tests; pass@1 is the usual headline number
best_model: Claude Opus 4.6 (vendor-reported, listed by Codesota; self-reported)
saturated_note: Launch best: Codex 28.8% (2021-07), GPT-3 0%. GPT-4 67.0% 0-shot in 2023-03 (OpenAI tech report, self-reported). First 90%+ found: GPT-4o 90.2% in 2024-05 (Codesota listing, self-reported; an earlier 90% by another model is unconfirmed). Codesota's aggregate page also shows o4-mini 97.3%, which conflicts with the 96.3% on its benchmark page (unconfirmed which is current). Known issues: tests are weak (EvalPlus added 80x more tests and cut pass@k by up to 19.3-28.9% across 26 LLMs, and changed rankings); problems have been public since 2021 and are widely mirrored so contamination is likely. Codesota calls it saturated. Label-error ceiling: unconfirmed.

org: Google (Austin et al.; affiliation not shown on the arXiv abstract page)
tests: Entry-level Python programming problems written by crowd workers, from a short English description.
format: Code generation: natural-language task description in, short Python program out; 3 assert tests per task
scoring: pass@k via the assert tests; pass@1 usual (often 3-shot)
best_model: o4-mini (listed by Codesota; undated; self-reported/aggregator, unconfirmed against OpenAI)
saturated_note: Launch: largest models 59.6% few-shot (2021-08, self-reported in the paper). Top aggregator score 94.9% (MBPP) and 88.2% MBPP+ (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct); dates not given, so the first-90% date is unconfirmed. Known issues: EvalPlus found MBPP+ needed broken tasks removed (399 -> 378 tasks, 2024-04) and fixed wrong ground-truth solutions for task IDs 459, 102, 559 (2024-06); it adds 35x more tests. Contamination likely (public since 2021). Qwen3 base reports use MBPP 3-shot (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Base 81.4).

org: UC Berkeley, MIT and Cornell (unconfirmed; authors listed without affiliations on the pages I fetched)
tests: Competitive-programming problems (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces) collected continuously after model training cutoffs; also self-repair, test-output prediction and code execution scenarios.
questions: Original 400 (2023-05 to 2024-05 window in paper abstract); release_v5 880; release_v6 1,055 (through 2025-04)
format: Code generation from problem statement; hidden tests
scoring: pass@1 (and pass@5) on hidden tests; results can be filtered by problem release date
best_score: 93.5% (version not stated on the model card)
best_date: 2026-04 (V4 release date per secondary sources, unconfirmed)
saturated_note: Contamination is handled by dating problems: score only problems released after a model's cutoff. Because the version/window differs between reports, scores are not comparable across papers (Qwen3 report: v5 window 2024.10-2025.02; Qwen3.5: v6; DeepSeek-V4: unstated). DeepSeek-V4-Flash Max 91.6 and V4-Pro High 89.8 are also near 90. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 83.6 (v6). First model to pass 90% on any version: unconfirmed. Default 'lite' set has pruned tests; errata kept in the repo (ERRATA.md).

org: Many universities and labs (authors listed without affiliations on the abstract page; org unconfirmed)
tests: Realistic scientific-computing code from physics, math, materials science, chemistry and biology research (16 subfields).
format: Code generation, each main problem split into dependent subproblems; scientist-written gold solutions and tests
scoring: Fraction of subproblems solved, and stricter main-problem accuracy (all subproblems must pass)
best_score: 66.9% (Artificial Analysis score on the 288 test subproblems; exact metric definition unconfirmed)
best_model: Claude Opus 5.5 (Max), independent Artificial Analysis run
saturated_note: Launch best: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.6% of main problems in the most realistic setting (2024-07, paper). Known issues: SciCode-Verified audit (arXiv 2608.04975, 2026-08-05) found 263 defects across all 65 test problems; 192 wrongly reject correct solutions, so published scores are underestimated; after fixes subproblem accuracy rose from ~45-60% to 84-98% and main-problem accuracy from ~9-27% to 69-92% on 12 frontier snapshots (author-reported). Artificial Analysis says it is reviewing and scores may change. So the real ceiling is near 100% but the public numbers are far lower.

org: OpenAI, with the Princeton SWE-bench authors (original SWE-bench: Princeton and collaborators)
tests: Fixing real GitHub issues in 12 popular Python repos; a model must edit the repo so hidden tests pass.
questions: 500 (human-filtered from 2,294 SWE-bench instances; 93 annotators screened 1,699 samples and 68.3% were filtered out)
format: Agentic: issue text + repository in, code patch out; the scaffold (agent loop and tools) matters
scoring: Resolved rate: FAIL_TO_PASS tests must pass and PASS_TO_PASS tests must still pass
human_baseline: None reported (annotators rated difficulty by estimated time)
best_score: 97.0% (independent, mini-SWE-agent bash-only harness); aggregators also list provider claims of 96%
best_model: Claude Opus 5, Vals AI independent run (leaderboard snapshot 2026-09-01; archived); the 96% provider figure is only seen on aggregators and Anthropic's Opus 5 page does not list SWE-bench Verified (unconfirmed)
saturated_note: Launch: best open scaffold with GPT-4o 33.2% (2024-08, OpenAI). Claude 3.7 Sonnet 63.7% no-scaffold, 70.3% with parallel-compute scaffold on 489 of 500 tasks (2025-02-24, self-reported). First 80%+: Claude Opus 4.5 80.9% (2025-11, vendor-reported; OpenAI later cited 80.9% as state of the art); GPT-5.2 80.0% (self-reported). First 90%+: unconfirmed date; Vals shows 96-97% by 2026. Open models: GLM-5 77.8% (OpenHands, self-reported), DeepSeek-V4-Pro Max 80.6%, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 76.4%. Known issues: OpenAI (2026-02-23) audited a hard 27.6% subset and found 59.4% of 138 problems had flawed tests or descriptions (35.5% narrow tests rejecting valid fixes, 18.8% too-wide tests), and every frontier model it tested could reproduce gold patches or details (contamination); OpenAI stopped reporting it and recommends SWE-bench Pro. Reports (secondary: Morph) say mini-swe-agent let agents read the gold fix from git history (21% on 100 tasks with Claude Opus 4.6); a Datacurve audit claim is unconfirmed. Vals marks it saturated. Scores depend heavily on scaffold and are not comparable across vendors.

org: Stanford University and the Laude Institute (Snorkel AI contributed)
tests: Hard, human-verified tasks run by an agent in a Docker terminal (software engineering, sysadmin, security etc.); 16 categories (4 easy, 55 medium, 30 hard).
format: Agentic: instruction + container in; tests check final container state only
scoring: Task resolution rate (all tests of a task must pass); results depend on agent harness and model
human_baseline: None reported (each task has a human-written oracle solution)
best_score: 84.7% (+/-2.1) Terminal-Bench leaderboard (hosted by Snorkel); independent Vals AI best 73.2%
best_model: NexAU-AHE agent + GPT-5.5 (leaderboard entry; whether the run was checked by the maintainers is unconfirmed); Vals AI: GPT 5.5 with Terminus 2 harness (run by Vals, 2026-06-04)
saturated_note: First >50%: Gemini 3 Pro 54.2% with Terminus-2 (as cited in the GLM-5 paper table; original report date about 2025-11, unconfirmed). Claude Opus 4.5 59.3 (Terminus-2) in the same table. Paper abstract (2026-01) says frontier agents were under 65%. Top 10 leaderboard entries span about 7 points with heavily overlapping 95% CIs. Known issues: GLM-5 reports a 'verified' fix of ambiguous task instructions (56.2 -> 60.7 Terminus-2); the authors aimed to keep frontier models under 50% but that no longer holds. Vals AI archived its run citing saturation; Terminal-Bench 4.0 is the successor, so 2.0 scores are not comparable with 4.0. BenchLM: 43 of 45 rows are provider self-reports (GPT-5.5 82%).
